utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in public session. Mr. O'Sullivan, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that you received a drip treatment in Mujo's room after being moved from the hangar. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you told us that the doctor inserted the needle into your arm to administer the treatment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your neighbour held the bottle from which the fluid was transfused into your body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at that point your condition was critical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you'd agree with me that it would be fair to say that before you received this drip treatment your condition was getting progressively worse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also agree with me that there were a number of factors that contributed to your condition: the stress, not eating and drinking adequately, the episode where a guard knocked your teeth out, and the fact that you spent much time outside on the pista.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you told us yesterday, it was while you were on the pista that you lost your teeth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that it was during the first month of your stay in Omarska that you were on the pista.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went from the pista to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also fair to say that before you were moved to the hangar, the place where you lost consciousness, you were in very bad shape on the pista.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in bad shape, especially until I was beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move on to a different area now. A moment ago you confirmed that you met twice with the Prosecution in 1995 and 1998, and it's correct that you told investigators from the Prosecution that based on the way the person you describe as Krle, based on the way he spoke, you thought that he was not from the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was what I thought, by the colour of his skin and so on, that he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the way he spoke.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 3/85D and 3/85D1, the photo boards. Can you place both of those pictures in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have in front of you photographs that are known as Prosecution Exhibit 3/85D1. Can you take a brief moment and look at all the faces once more. There's no need to focus on face number 4. I'll ask you to focus on the other faces, please. Have you had a chance to look at all the other faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from photo 4, not counting photo 4, you are able to recognise someone else, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not capable of recognising anyone else. I can't focus my mind back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does someone look familiar to you, other than number 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, no. Possibly he may have been there but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that? What number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them do not seem familiar. I can't say that any one of them was there now, except the one under number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You can remove the photos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you spoke about a man who was shot, in your words, you described him as a person who had lost his nerve and gone a bit crazy. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was my opinion, judging by the way he behaved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You arrived in Omarska on May 30th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that this shooting occurred over one month after you arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was sometime around then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you would agree with me that you have given three different dates concerning the date on which you say this shooting occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible. But to tell you the honest truth, I can't remember. It was a long time ago and we lost trace of the date down there, so I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1995 you told the Prosecution, when they interviewed you, that it happened on July 24th, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I might have said that, but I'm trying to forget that incident. I may have said that, because that interview was two or three years after the event, and now it's even further back in time, so I can't be certain about any date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1998 when you met with the Prosecutor, you said it happened 20 days after you arrived, which is June 20th. You said that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have said that, but I'm repeating: I'm not certain of the date. I know that the event happened and that I was present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, I apologise for interrupting you. The witness has given you an answer and you are insisting, so please move on to another question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have given different details about the person whom you say was shot; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, I didn't know the man, whether he was from Kozarac or Skela. But regarding the event I saw, I always described it in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in 1995 when you said he was from Kozarac, you made a mistake; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He may have been from Kozarac or Skela. To this day I don't know where he was from. He was not somebody I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in 1998 when you were interviewed by the Prosecution, you said that saying that this man was from Kozarac was a mistake. You told the Prosecution that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. O'Sullivan. It's the same observation I have to make to you. You are insisting. The witness has given you an answer. Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In addition, Your Honour, the Prosecution objects to the question as misleading, and on page 6 of this 1998 interview, the witness says: "In my previous statement, if it states that the person killed by Krle was from Kozarac, it is incorrect. I did not say that." So the witness doesn't say it was a mistake in the 1998 statement, he says he did not say that. And that is on page 6, sixth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, I understand that you have prepared your cross in a certain order, but the second part of this must be eliminated as soon as you get an answer from the witness. So you mustn't insist. Please move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Hollis quite correctly points out that the witness says that it was incorrect. I'm asking the witness if he made a mistake. That's the basis for asking that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is, sir: When you told the Prosecution it was Kozarac, were you mistaken?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I'm going to object. In the 1998 statement, the witness says, "I never said it was Kozarac." So he's making it appear as though the witness said something the witness has denied in the statement saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I remind you what you said in 1995. You said, and I quote, referring to the victim: "He came from Kozarac." That is what you said in your 1995 statement. My question is: Did you make a mistake when you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm saying again: I don't remember mentioning that. That may be a mistake. I still don't know where that man was from, and it didn't interest me. It was an astonishment for me to see a man being killed in front of my very eyes, for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put this to you: You saw Krle in Omarska when you were there, but you are mistaken when you say he shot someone. Do you accept that possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my conviction, I do not accept, because he came at five or six minutes later, the man went towards him, he went towards the man. He raised his gun. I heard the shots. The man fell. In my conviction, as I was watching, it was Krle who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. O'Sullivan. It is now the turn of Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, you spoke at length yesterday, so we need to go over a few points to clear them up. A moment ago, talking to Mr. O'Sullivan, you said that you do not remember dates in view of the conditions, which is quite understandable. But I do appeal to you nevertheless, because dates are important here for the truth, and thereby also for justice, that you do make an extra effort and, regarding certain events, try as best you can to place them in time, the time when they occurred, of course, as far as you're able.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I shall do my best, but I am just not able to determine the dates now, because, anyway, I'm trying to forget these things. I find it hard even to think about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you arrived in Omarska on the 30th of May, 1992, in the late afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You also said that you came by bus.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we came with AutoTransport buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please answer me as briefly as possible because that will speed things up. How many buses were there in your column; can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were three buses when I was getting on but the buses were coming and going. But when I got on, there were three buses, and my bus was the second in the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So from the starting point, there were three buses, when you were getting on, and then new buses arrived. Can we agree that your bus was the second?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who escorted you, who provided security, whatever you like, in your bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my bus I seemed to have recognised him. I don't know the name. Drazo who used to work in Prijedor, he was a driver, and as far as I can see, it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: The person escorting you, was there only one or several?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several, but when we got in we had to bend down our heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There may have been three or four, but I saw him as we entered. He was the driver. And I knew him from the lotto in Prijedor. And there were military persons around.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were those people in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drazo was in a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Civilian or military police? Because you do understand those things.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the regular blue police uniform. It wasn't a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When you came to Omarska, you said that your bus stopped at the level of Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: At that particular moment, were there any other buses in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were not, because our bus stopped by the SUP building before going on to Omarska. I forgot to say that, perhaps. And one man got out and came back and joined us, and I saw that -- I didn't actually see, but I saw that it was in front of the SUP. And then we went off in an unknown direction, I didn't know where we were going, but then we arrived in Omarska. So I saw that one bus when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please try and answer my questions. If you wish to add anything, any essential point, you can of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think that it is essential that we stopped off on the way at one particular place and then went on. You judge whether it's essential or not yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. But I didn't get an answer to my previous question. In front of you, were there other buses when you stopped in Omarska, in front of Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there was only my own bus. That's as far as I can remember. Just my bus, the bus I got out of.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So that means that at that point in time, there was only your bus.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only my bus. And another bus arrived later on, my one left, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the bus that was going in front of you, that was in front of you? Where did that bus go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You don't know, you say. Very well. Yesterday you said that when you got out that you were searched, that is to say, all the people who had been taken into custody were searched, and that a list was compiled, that some valuables were taken from some people. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who conducted this search? Were they the individuals who escorted you or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that when we came we had to stand up against this wall, and I didn't see who was conducting the search. We weren't allowed to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Who took a note of your names? Was it one of the people who escorted you? You must have seen that because you were looking at the man whom you were speaking to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time the man was not somebody I knew. He had a blue uniform on and he wrote it all down. If I knew who it was, I would tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Later on, during the time you spent in Omarska, and you were there for about 66 days, I believe, did you happen to see that man as being a member of the Omarska police, who provided security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that I saw him but --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You said a moment ago, on two occasions, uniforms -- you said yesterday that you were a member of the army and that you had the rank of private first class. Does that mean that you know something about uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I should know something, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: There is a difference between military and police uniforms, is there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Is that difference such that your ordinary citizen can differentiate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The militia had a light blue shirt and dark blue trousers, we knew that was the civilian police, whereas the military had the SMB olive-green/grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned military and police camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was there a difference between the police camouflage uniforms and the military camouflage uniforms, army ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a difference did exist, because the SMB olive-green/grey is the army type and the camouflage police uniform was light blue and dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. You were in the army. Did the army have its own police force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. I know that it did --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Let's just keep it brief. Us ordinary citizens, especially those of us who had done our military service, and 90 per cent did do their military service in our country, in town how were we able to differentiate between an army policeman and a civilian policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was an army police uniform, he had the belt, the white belt. And that was the difference for traffic control and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So military policemen had white belts, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I shall return to the question of uniforms in a moment, and I shall be talking about Mr. Kvocka in that regard. You said yesterday that when you saw him first in Omarska that he was wearing a standard blue police uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say "standard," I said it was a camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: But you said a blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. But was that a police camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he remain in that uniform until his departure from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I think he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I mentioned Mr. Kvocka's departure. Perhaps we should deal with that matter now and not go back to it later on. Do you know the reason for his departure from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You do not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never learnt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Now let us go back once again to the question of your arrival at Omarska, in the evening of the 30th of May, 1992. When you were searched and your name taken down, where did you go first from the bus? Where were you taken and put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the pista, that is to say, the area between the restaurant --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. We'll clarify what we mean by the pista on the basis of photographs. We'll do that later on. Thank you. Were there any people out on the pista when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Well, make a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps there were some 50 to 100 people at that particular moment. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: While you were out on the pista, what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I sat around --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You were sitting. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you see the arrival of fresh buses? How many other buses arrived and how many people got out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't -- I don't know the number of buses. Buses did arrive. There were beatings and screams --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I'm asking you how many buses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number. I didn't pay sufficient attention to that, but buses did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How many people would there be per bus, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depends, but 50 to 60 people in normal times. It depends on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where did these new arrivals go to? When they left the bus, where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them would join us, and others went to other premises. I didn't follow this all the time, where they were being distributed. At that moment it was a surprise for me to be where I was. I didn't know, actually, that I was in Omarska because I'd never been to Omarska before, so I didn't pay attention to details like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yesterday I reacted to one of your statements, that is to say, the way in which you presented it, so I'm going to clarify this point for the Trial Chamber by asking additional questions through this cross-examination, and try to clarify some matters. You mentioned that the buses that came later, that from these buses -- that in these buses two of your neighbours arrived, and that they got out of the buses beaten up and that they said that they had been at the police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but at that moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just give me an answer. So your answer is yes there. Thank you. Could you give us their names, place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ismet Okic and Hamdija Brkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Ismet Okic and Amir Brkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Hamdija.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Hamdija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where were they put up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that we had already been taken into what had been called Mujo's room. I was in Mujo's room at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. At that particular time you say you were in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just slowly. I know you were taken in there, but let's take it step by step. How did you see them getting out of the buses beaten up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they told me that their bus had stopped off at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: But you said yesterday that you saw them getting out of the bus beaten up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You did say that. You said it again a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go back to the question that was asked by my distinguished colleague, Madam Hollis, and it is page 48, line 24 of the transcript, and that's how I understood his statement. "I think he told us his name but I'm not sure --" no, I apologise. I've made a mistake. Let us go back. Madam Hollis yesterday said that they had gone into the room and that they were beaten up, and so the conclusion is that they were beaten up in the dormitory, in Mujo's room. Were they beaten in Mujo's room or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. The answer is no, which means that these two individuals did come to Mujo's room, you contacted with them the first time and they told you that they had been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I see. In SUP. That evening, was anybody else beaten in Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Mujo's room, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he was or not, because I came in late.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know Half Berek and the teacher Mr. Oklopcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know him because I know him as a football player. I would always watch football games.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, 1992, was he together with you in Mujo's dormitory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember whether we were there together, because up until that moment we would be taken out -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So you don't know whether you saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see him that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let us return to the question of the pista. You went into Mujo's room a moment ago too quickly. I'm speaking figuratively, of course. Witness AI, how long were you on the pista after you got out of the bus and were searched, up until the time, as you state, you were addressed by Mr. Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about two hours, an hour or two. I was on the pista for that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you ever see him before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: That means -- can we agree that you saw Mr. Kvocka for the first time, as you say, in that particular contact on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How did Mr. Kvocka address you? Did he just address you yourself personally, or the whole group of 200, 300 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he addressed us in the following way -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I'm asking whether he addressed just you or the whole group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He addressed all of us, said that everything would be all right, that we would be interrogated and returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Yesterday you said, and that is page 48 now, "Yes, that is how I understood his statement. I think he told us his name but I'm not sure. But never mind. Later on I learnt that his name was Kvocka." Witness AI, are you quite sure, in view of the doubt that you yourself express when asked by Ms. Hollis, that he addressed you and introduced himself by giving his name and surname? When you say that "I later learnt of that"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He introduced himself, Kvocka, but I didn't pay much attention to him. I just remember his face. And then when we talked amongst ourselves, I realised that that was that man. But he did address -- introduce himself but he didn't say his name --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. A moment ago you said "I didn't remember his image, his face."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that. I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. So you said that you didn't notice his face that evening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't remember it much. I saw the face but I didn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yes, you said you saw the face but didn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because it was all a surprise to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that's the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You have already confirmed that in the course of August 1995 you gave a statement to the representatives of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did the gentleman who took your statement introduce himself by giving his name and surname and his official function; yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He -- possibly he did introduce himself but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did his associate introduce herself, who was with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she did not. She just at moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She just went in and came out. Came in and went out, sort of. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, how long on that particular day did you spend talking to, and I'm going to tell you his name, to Mr. Grant Niemann, a very distinguished lawyer and experienced one? How long did you discuss things with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps 20 minutes to half an hour. I wasn't there for long. Twenty minutes, half an hour. I don't know how long exactly I was in there. But he didn't abuse me in any way or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Therefore, that means that we can agree on one point: that you and Mr. Niemann talked for about 20 minutes, and that during that time your statement was translated, printed out, typed out, that it was read back to you in English, that you signed it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please let me finish. And that in the English version, you even --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, I think that you are drawing too many conclusions. Ask your questions of the witness and let him answer. Say, "How long did --" what I was saying was the following: Ask questions one by one. Don't make the conclusions yourself. The witness gave you an answer, and he said that he spent 20 minutes in the interview. Now, leave the conclusions to the end. Ask your questions first, otherwise you're going to enter into an argument with the witness. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I have an answer to make. When he asked me, I thought that he meant the interrogator in Omarska, and that is why I said 20 minutes, half an hour. I didn't understand his question. So I'd like to clear that point up. I thought you were talking about Omarska. I thought counsel was asking me about Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Witness. Mr. Simic will restate his question to clarify matters. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, how long did the interviews last between you and Mr. Niemann on the 16th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but it was rather a lengthy conversation. I can't tell you the exact time, how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Well, was it one working day, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, not the whole working day, but, you know, time passes very quickly when you're doing that sort of thing. I was speaking freely and so on. Before that I thought you were asking about the Omarska interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. I accept your explanation there, on that point. That was August of 1995; that means three years after the end of that unfortunate Omarska affair. Did you, on that occasion, remember more fully, better, the events, in view of the fact that it was closer to the time when it had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would say I remembered it better, yes. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I should now like to ask the witness to be shown the statement of August 1995, and at the same time to distribute one copy of the English version to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, just one moment, please. Before we continue, can we have the number of that exhibit? I would like to have the number of the document. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are just presenting a piece of evidence and we'll later decide whether we're going to tender it into evidence for admission, after the talk with the witness. Yesterday you said we would assign numbers at the end of the hearing. But according to our records, this is D59, this document has been assigned the number D59. But it is not the Defence Exhibits that have already been tendered, they are the ones that have come up. But let me facilitate matters for the transcript and the record, we expect that the registrar will assign it a definite number later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said yesterday was that we're going to discuss the admissibility of documents at the end. But while we're working with a document, we have to identify that document and that is why I'm asking, now the registrar, to give us a number for that document. Whether it will be tendered into evidence and admitted or not, that is another matter. But you're talking about a piece of paper and we don't know what it is. So if we give it a number, it is identified. It can be tendered later on and admitted later on; that's another question. But madam registrar, may have I the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D25/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Simic, we now have the number; it is D25/1. And now you can always refer to the document by that number and we'll all know what document you're talking about. Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Simic. I apologise for interrupting you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, would you look at page 2 of that document, and you have underlined in green the portion that I wish to discuss with you. In the talk with Mr. Niemann, in your conversation with Mr. Niemann, in paragraph 4 you state the following: [as interpreted] "Some of the guards in Omarska whom I remember were: Kvocka (which means hen); Pop (which means Priest); Ckalja, the shift leader; Krkan; Zeljko Meakic, the camp commander; Zoran Zigic; Dusko Tadic; Slobodan Dosen; Vojvoda (means duke); Sasa Stjepic, he only came occasionally." Have you found that passage in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I was able to follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was that statement clearly read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I should now like to ask the usher to give me the English version back again for a moment, because there's a detail that I have to refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, Mr. Simic, in the meantime, Mr. Simic, I would like to take advantage of this interruption to say that it is a good idea to underline the paragraph that you're working with and asking the witness about. This is very good procedure for the future, to identify. So it's a very good idea of yours to have underlined the passage that you're concerned with for the witness' and our benefit. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, did Mr. Niemann, as a highly conscientious and responsible person, when the statement was read out to you, did he ask you to initial the correction next to the name "Zeljko Meakic"? Look at the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these are my initials. My initials, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't written -- spelt correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So the only correction had to do with the spelling of the name of Mr. Meakic. Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I don't need the document any more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: As we were speaking about your statement, in which, of your own free will, you described Mr. Kvocka as a guard that you remember, let us continue with questions about Mr. Kvocka. Did he have any relatives in Omarska? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was another guard who was called Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know whom Kvocka is married to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I later learnt that he was married to someone from Skela.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What ethnicity is his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I heard, whether it's true or not. That was in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, were there relatives of Kvocka's wife in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Whether there were or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know somebody called Trta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Trta, yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You said here that you learnt from Mr. Trta that the brothers of Kvocka's wife were in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible that I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the objection, Mr. Nikolic? I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript. In answer to a question, the witness answered what ethnicity Mr. Kvocka's wife was, but it didn't appear in the transcript. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What ethnicity was Mr. Kvocka's wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I knew, she was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Nikolic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Talking about Mr. Kvocka, let us clarify a few other details. In one of your statements you mentioned, or rather you stated, that Mr. Kvocka occasionally came to Omarska in a white Mercedes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible that it was a white Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What type?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the older models. 200D, I think, not the new models.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, we're talking about the year 1992. There was a new model -- so it was an old model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was a classical type of old Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: My assistant who knows the models said that they were the old 123.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the models of Mercedes. I'm not in that category.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let's go back to your first 10- or 15-day stay in Omarska. You stated yesterday that during the first 10 or 15 days people were not mistreated, that some people even volunteered to be interrogated, that some people after those interrogations were released home. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you try and estimate the number of people who were released to go home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. At the beginning that is true, some people were interrogated and then released.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: But can you tell us, did this happen throughout those first 10 or 15 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't remember. But it is true that some were released. There were cases of people being released. Where they went, I don't know. Whether they went home or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: But, anyway, they left Omarska. As far as you know, they went home, but you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You spoke at length about seeing bodies in Omarska. Fully appreciating your problem with determining dates, in view of the terrible experiences you went through which I deeply regret, could you say that during those first 10 or 15 days, was there violence and bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think the second or third night, somebody was killed in the restaurant. I didn't mention it yesterday. I don't know who did the killing, and that is why I didn't mention it. A man was beaten up in front of the restaurant too.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. So on the second or third night after your arrival, a person was killed in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I should now like to go back to an event that you described in some detail yesterday. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P3/83. So I should like to ask the usher for his assistance. Yesterday you were commenting and marking on this photograph with "X", indicating one person, and Mr. KV, Kvocka, as the other person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You stated that you were at the pista, that the situation was normal, you were talking, sitting there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you describe this young man "X"? As far as I can see, he's coming from the entrance and going towards the pista; is that correct? And can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure about describing him. He was in a military uniform. I didn't look at him closely. He was yelling. He would come earlier on --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. So you can't describe his face, but you can describe, or rather confirm, that he was wearing a military uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: A moment ago we were talking about military policemen or an ordinary soldier. Could you notice that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember he was wearing a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did he have a belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't have a white belt. No, he didn't. I didn't notice that at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you not pay attention, or was he not wearing a white belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't really pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: This area in front of you on the photograph, was any other guard present there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were guards. Kvocka was talking to some guards here at the entrance, and there were guards there, the people who were watching over us.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you recognise any one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say now which shift it was, Krle's or Krkan's. I can't remember the details. I just remember this man coming and yelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You remember that a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is still in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you see this young man talking to anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. That is what I saw that moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Where is Mujo's room in relation to this first "X"? Behind his back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the garage. At the end of this -- there's the garage and then comes Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: The garage and then Mujo's room, so we agree on that. This person is moving from Mujo's room towards the pista.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not from Mujo's room. When I saw him --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Is he moving away from Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was coming from the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And when you're coming from the gate, you have to pass by Mujo's room and the garage. Will you look at the monitor, please? Is the gate -- will you show us where the gate is, to simplify matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this direction [indicates], over there. It's not on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying too. So he's coming from the gate, passing Mujo's room, and approaching you to call out people, without talking to anyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see him talking to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that he went to Mujo's room, I just said where I saw him. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Let us now go back for a moment to the mentioned -- the bodies you mentioned. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] And D5/61, it is a photograph, and we are producing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I think that we have to be quite clear now. Mr. Simic mentioned D5/61. Is that the official mark of the Registrar? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] No, it is our new marking. It is evidence that we are producing for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, it still doesn't have an official number. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] But it is our number, it is the number we gave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that is your business, but not for all of us. For us it is the Registrar who has to mark it. So to avoid all confusion, as you see, the registrar was looking for the exhibit and it doesn't exist in the file. So let's be careful. The exhibit doesn't exist in our file; it is the first time that it is going to be produced. Therefore, you have to give it an official marking now. So in future you will say, "I wish to produce this document," without giving it any number, otherwise there will be disastrous confusion. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Before, that was how we proceeded, and I was acting in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no point in looking for it. Yes, you're right, Mr. Simic. Never mind. Madam Registrar, how will this new document be marked, the one that Mr. Simic, the Defence attorney of Mr. Kvocka, wishes to produce? Will you identify it now, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Normally if it is the exhibits used for Kvocka, then it should be "/1". So there is no such number like this, such as "/65".

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It should be D26. The last one was D25. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the registrar has been notified of certain Defence exhibits, but as the Defence has not started its case, all the exhibits have not been produced which we intend to use, and there are new ones that are coming. And the Registrar is trying to find this exhibit among those that I have already disclosed, but this is a completely new exhibit appearing in the Tribunal for the first time, and it just needs to be marked for identification. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is what we have been waiting for for some time, that the registrar tells us the number of this exhibit which is being produced for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sir, are you telling me that this is a new exhibit you're going to tender to the Court? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a new document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay. So the number is going to be D26/1. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Could the document be shown to Witness AI, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I also have some more copies of this? Because I only have one copy of that. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I'm afraid we have no further copies. We got this document from the Prosecution and we didn't have the technical possibility of reproducing it. But we'll deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can produce copies later. But for the moment it has to be registered with the Registry, and it has now been marked as D26/1. So please continue, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You mentioned the pista frequently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can we agree that it is an area, the edges of which were marked by these concrete flower pots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Now, let us describe the boundaries of it. You see the policeman standing there; you see the first, if we can call it, flower pot, concrete flower pot. Does that mean that the borders of the pista, I'm referring in relation to the "white house," begins from the entrance to the restaurant or the central administrative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Those flower pots were along the side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So the restaurant was not part of the pista. I think you understand what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The restaurant was in front of me, and I was on the pista, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you were sitting next to the wall of the hangar most often. From that position, is it possible to see the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Having mentioned the "white house," yesterday you stated that you never saw Mr. Kvocka entering the "white house."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let me go back again now to the statement you gave on the 18th of September, 1998. On that occasion, did the person taking the statement from you introduce himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know who was the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think her name was Aida.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was that statement given in the same way to Mr. Niemann, of your own free will, professionally, without any kind of pressure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Without any pressure or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you again sign that statement in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So the procedure was the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So as not to waste time, let me quote two lines from your statement: "Many times I saw Kvocka entering the white house. I don't know what he was doing there. He would usually stay inside 10 to 15 minutes. I remember he was also escorted by a guard."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need any explanations. To finish with this statement, a moment ago you explicitly stated that you saw Mr. Kvocka for the first time on the 30th of May, 1992 when he came to you and the other prisoners on the pista. I have to remind you again of your statement from 1998. This will speed things up. I want to finish by the break. "The first evening when we arrived at the camp, Kvocka was present, when they searched us and beat us. When they beat the prisoners and took our personal belongings, we had to bend our heads and we were ordered not to look around." Did you sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I said that he didn't beat me. Maybe it was translated differently. They were beating others but not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I'm just saying what you stated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stated that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: We are back to the 30th of May, 1992. That evening, did something happen which was out of the usual? Did you see or hear anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard but I didn't see that there were beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So you just heard buses come and beatings. That is all I asked you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was shooting too, but I'm not sure of that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Will you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was shooting too, but I didn't see where it came from. I don't want to enter into any details that I'm not sure of. I want to forget much of those things. I don't care about these people here. It's Drazenko Predojevic who did me the worst evil, and I would like to reach him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let us bring things to a close. You said yesterday that you saw Kvocka talking to the guards and moving around.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- I never said I saw him hit anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Very well. But did you ever hear that he gave orders to anyone to kill or to beat or anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never heard him say any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, just a couple of questions more. Are you familiar with the organisation of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How it functions, the services, the head of departments, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know how the chain of command goes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know there must be chiefs and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know how these people are appointed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the president of the municipality who would appoint them, but I don't know any more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Witness AI, I have no further questions for you. Thank you once again, and I must say how deeply I regret what you went through once again, and I hope that you will recover fully, as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I would like too, to regain my strength. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] We would like to tender the statement from 1994 as an exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll consider that at the end of the entire cross-examination. Is that all right? I think now it is Mr. Fila's turn, but I think we first have to have a break. I think this is a good time for the break. It is two minutes to eleven. So we're going to have a half hour break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. We are going to resume the hearing with the cross-examination of Witness AI by Mr. Fila. But I see Mr. Simic on his feet. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one comment or objection to the transcript that I have received from my colleagues, and that is that it wasn't introduced into the LiveNote, Witness AI's statement, when he decisively stated that he had nothing against Mr. Kvocka. So in order to avoid any misunderstandings, I should like this to be corrected in the LiveNote, or to be reinserted, reconfirmed by the witness himself, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We all heard that, and everyone interpreted what the witness said. It is true that the witness did say that, and we have taken due note of it. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, you have the floor, and you may start off with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I should be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In your testimony -- first of all, good morning, Witness, Witness AI. I don't like using the initials, but anyway. You said at the start of your testimony that when you came on the 30th of May, there were military men and special units from Banja Luka, and later on you spoke about the guards as well. Now, are these three different things you're talking about, or were these elite units and the army the same? Could you tell me a little more about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the special police, the special police unit that was there. And after a certain amount of time they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well. That's one point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Second, the guards. The guards were those who were wearing uniforms. Some had military uniforms, others had police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So there were two categories: these special units and the guards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But a third category --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, well, the army. What do you mean by a third category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a third category, the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So there wasn't anything --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as I say, there was the special police unit and these others in these mixed uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well, we've cleared that point up. Now, I'm interested in the following: These special units, do you know under whose command they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did the guard -- was the guard in command of these special units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So that's another point. You don't know the relationship between the special units who came and went and the guards that were there until the end, all the time you were there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did some of these people have green uniforms, camouflage uniforms or ordinary green uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had the army olive-green/grey uniforms. The guards did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now, those wearing those olive-green uniforms, did you see them throughout your stay there or did they go off somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the guards had these -- both these uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But what about the army? I'm interested in the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. I can't remember the details of who was wearing what and who belonged to which forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Sir, please don't tell me anything you don't remember, and I don't mind if you tell me that you don't remember. And I would find it very strange if I were to remember anything in those circumstances either, so I do understand. The next question I'm interested in is the following: You said that someone seems to have done the schedules for the guards and shifts in advance. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the leader of the shift knew which guard would be assigned to which position, so that's what I meant, where they would be on duty, on guard duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were always the same people in the same spots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But it wasn't as you did the thing, that you would say, "You go there and you go here," but they knew this in advance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify what you meant when you said that. Would you now explain the following to us: What would a shift look like, that is to say, how did the shifts replace each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember the shift would come in by bus, they would walk in a column and they took up their posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What about the previous shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The previous shift would go away. And they would come up towards the restaurant mostly and then would go into the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mean the shift that was leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know where Krkan was standing? Where did he move around? Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would see him walking around. He didn't have any set post or position where he stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you ever see him go to the restaurant? Did you ever see him go up -- go through that protrusion there on the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I saw him go there, into the restaurant, he would walk around the pista, and so on. He didn't have a set position.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In that glass house, did you see him standing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't follow him around, of course, but I would see him. When I see him, I see him, depending on where he was, whether he was in the restaurant or elsewhere, inside the restaurant, by the restaurant, wherever.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mean this glass semicircular partition, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You told us that Drazenko Predojevic beat you for some reason but you didn't know why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, I didn't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did he do this following orders? Did somebody come and order him to hit someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see him ordered by anyone, by the shift leader or anybody else. I can't say that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was it necessary for anybody to order somebody to beat one of the detainees, or did they beat them at random?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my conclusion is that they beat them at random.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Will you agree with me, then, that it was a state of anarchy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I don't know whether they were told to or not. I didn't hear anybody order one of them to beat the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you complain to anybody about Drazenko Predojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't dare complain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well, then. That means you did not complain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During the time you spent in Omarska, where was your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went home, I learnt that they had been in the Raskovic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In Prijedor, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were they harmed by anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my father told me later on that they searched the house and that they looted him once and that his ID card was found in another house later on. So things like that did happen, and that's what my father told me happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you were released, you went to that house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the last seven to ten days of your stay in Omarska, did the situation improve at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I was able to remember, a little bit. There wasn't so much beating going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When did you leave Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, on the 6th --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And ten days before that, the situation had improved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, but the beatings did go on, the roll-calls did go on, but I felt that it was slightly better. I felt a little safer where I was in those last days, but what actually happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When the shifts would replace each other, apart from what you have just described, the replacement of shifts, that is to say, one shift leaving and another arriving, was there anything else when you were on the pista? What did you do on the pista? What did you do on the pista while the shifts were taking each other's turn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depends. We would have to lie down on our stomachs --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm just interested in the shifts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when the shift would come, if there had been beatings, we would all be told to lie face down on the pista and we would do this for hours at times. And I wasn't able to see the details. I can't remember anything special.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let me help you. Was there a ceremony of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So it was just that one shift arrived and the other shift left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did this happen in the morning and in the evening, that is to say, did the shifts replace each other in the morning and in the evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was in the restaurant --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm asking you when you saw this. If you didn't see anything, don't tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, had I seen anything, I would tell you, but I didn't actually see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you didn't notice any ceremony taking place when the shifts replaced each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all from me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fila. It is now Mr. Tosic's team who has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honours. The order of the cross-examination will be done by myself and Mr. Tosic, we shall take turns. But I will start off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself to the witness, I'm attorney Slobodan Stojanovic from Belgrade, and I'm one of the Defence counsel from Mr. Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have a clarification on that? Is it going to be permitted that more than one counsel from a team will be permitted to question a witness? Because we object to that. That could permits lead to ten people examining a witness. In our submission it should be one person from each team who is allowed to question the witness. We thought that was what had already been discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honour. Let me clarify that. No, I shall only be asking questions of the witness. Just one member from our team. So that was a misunderstanding. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness AI, it is not customary to address people in that way, but I shall respect this rule and address you as "AI." And I hope you will help the Defence in arriving at the truth by your answers. We shall adhere to a sequence of events which you talk about in both your written statements and in your oral testimony. I think that in the first statement it says that on the 30th of May, 1992 Prijedor was attacked. Can you tell us something about that? Why was Prijedor attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, why it was attacked, I think it was to liberate Prijedor, and power was taken over forcefully. But I wasn't interested in politics so I don't know the details of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who attacked Prijedor? Whose forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I don't know. And later on I met -- there was this Slavko, but I didn't know him, so I can't really say which army attacked. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, when your father's house -- when the shooting started, I think you said that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- and I think that you said you felt safer in that place. Does that mean that you expected some shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. But before that there was some shooting, whether it was at Kozarac, I don't know the details, so that we gathered together in my father's house. We felt safer there because there were women and children there, and that's why we gathered there, for safety reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honour, I should like to ask an exceptionally important question now by your leave, that is to say, I'd like my client Zoran Zigic to get up so that we can pose a very direct question. And our client insists on this especially. Do we have your permission for him to rise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. I think the Prosecution carried out the procedure of identification, and we must mirror this procedure in the cross-examination. So you can ask the witness, and there are no questions that are more or less important here in this courtroom. There are only questions. So please say questions without saying that this is a very important question. All questions are questions. Please go ahead, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was just making an explanation, but I accept your ruling, of course. Therefore, my client Zoran Zigic today is dressed the way the SMB olive-grey uniform, and he would like to ask -- that is, I would like to ask, is this gentleman here the individual who called out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to this statement that this accused is dressed like the SMB uniform. That is a statement of fact. The attorney cannot testify. If the attorney wishes to ask the client if any -- the witness if anyone in the room is dressed like that, we suggest that would be appropriate. But we do object to a flat statement that anyone in this room is dressed like the SMB uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't say he was wearing that particular clothing, but that the colour is similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you can ask the witness the following question: What was your client dressed like? You cannot put answers into his mouth and plead instead of him. So you can ask him how your client is or was dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I won't be asking that question. Let me ask a direct question, then. I shall point to Mr. -- I think that that is the gentleman in the first row, he is sitting to the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the gentleman who called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. Excuse me, Mr. Stojanovic. I think that you are obstructing our work here at the moment. We have just said that you cannot say that your client is dressed in such and such a way. You cannot say that your client is in the first row either, on the right-hand side. You must ask the witness whether he sees your client or not. Do you understand what I'm getting at? Do you understand what we're trying to point out here, Mr. Stojanovic? You are insisting upon the same point that we have not authorised you to do. Check whole exchange with SM.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me restate the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please do reformulate the question. Go ahead, ask your question, put your question to it, but do not elicit an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does the witness see in this courtroom the individual who called Kiki, Rezak, and Began Beganovic out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember his face exactly. I didn't look at him too much. And I don't know him, I don't recognise him, and I don't wish to speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
