As to the second point, if I can make a general observation and not limit it to this specific instance raised by Mr. Fila. Your Honours, under Rule 85(B), it is clear that the parties, as well as Your Honours, may question a witness. Rule 5(A) is equally clear to the extent that an objection must be made at the earliest opportunity. In my submission, when a witness is questioned and a party has an objection to the form of questioning, regardless of who the questioner is, Rule 5 clearly states that that objection must be made as soon as possible, and Rule 5 is not limited in its scope and, in my submission, covers questioning under Rule 85(B). Those, it seems to me, are the parameters of this issue, and it's in that context that objections must be made according to our Rules whenever a party feels that there is a basis for an objection, regardless of who is asking the question. Those are my submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. O'Sullivan. Mr. Tosic. Mr. Stojanovic, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections to make with respect to the proposed exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Jovan Simic. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, therefore, that there are no objections with respect to the tendering of D25/1, so that the exhibits have all been tendered. I think that we ought to give a little thought on the question that was raised as well. I stand by the position that I indicated to you, but we shall have some reflection on the subject. We have 20 more minutes for hearing or starting to hear another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution would call Witness B to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I could take advantage of the opportunity to hear how many witnesses you still have this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have two, including Witness B, here, but it's our estimation that it's very unlikely, using the normal work schedule, that we will conclude both witnesses. In fact, it would be my estimation at this time that we would only conclude Witness B. That was the issue that we would like to raise afterwards with respect to whether the Judges would desire to go extra time both days to try and conclude both witnesses. But in my estimation, it would probably mean an additional two hours each day in order to conclude both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two hours each day; that is to say, today and tomorrow, two extra hours per day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That would be my estimation, Your Honour, based on just the way we have proceeded with the witnesses thus far this week, and I see no reason to indicate the timing would be any different for the next two. They're both fairly significant witnesses. If the Defence has another opinion on it, I'd be happy to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the viewpoint of the Defence with respect to doing our utmost to set the witnesses free? And we're going to interrupt ... MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I still feel that there might be an unrealistic assessment. We have witnesses here before us; we have had days behind us and know what it looks like. And as the witness is an important one, he has a lengthy statement, lengthy testimony, and I think that we'll have to bring him back. We discussed this, to have the two witnesses back, and today and tomorrow to get through with Witness B. That is, perhaps, more realistic but it's up to you to decide. I don't know whether this speeding up of matters will necessarily lead to the proper results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that opinion shared by the other Defence counsel, or are there differing opinions? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might. There is one additional factor. I know you're concerned about the issue of how long witnesses are here. This witness, in fact, only arrived last night -- the second witness, not Witness B, but the one who would follow her. So he, in fact, has not been here that long, Witness AL. There is also a concern, however, whether or not he would be willing to come back a second time, but that's something that we'll have to address depending on your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan. The problem is, as you can well understand, a whole series of questions with respect to all the people working here, not maybe in the courtroom but who are the support of all of us here, and we too have constraints. I myself, for example, have something at 3.15, a meeting that I cannot put off, and another one tomorrow of the same nature. So that is a pity. My colleagues, the Judges, would like to continue, but of course there are these constraints and we must foresee all this in advance to be able to function properly. So we're going to go as far as possible, do as much as possible, but quite certainly we cannot hear just one -- we may be able to hear just one witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards protective measures, Mr. Keegan, for this witness, what are they, Witness B?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Pseudonym, Your Honour, obviously, and facial distortion. And of course we would want the initial session in private session as we go through just the basic biographical data, and then after that the normal session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're now going to -- Mr. O'Sullivan, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Just to make sure that Your Honours are correctly informed. At the break Mr. Keegan spoke with us, and of course there is always perhaps a language barrier between Mr. Keegan and some of my colleagues who don't speak English, my understanding was that the sensible solution for the second witness may, in fact, be to tell that witness that it's not likely that he would begin his examination-in-chief before the end of tomorrow, and if he did he would be two weeks before he came back to complete his examination-in-chief. So that was our understanding, under Mr. Keegan's suggestion, and I think I'm speaking correctly that it may be the sensible solution, for the benefit of the second witness, to do our best to complete the witness who is about to enter. I just wanted to state that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and that's what we said, I think. Was there a difference on your side as to what we said? We said that it was better only to hear this witness and to inform the other witness that we cannot hear his testimony at this point. So we're going to introduce one witness and we're going to do our best to hear that witness today and tomorrow, because we only have ten more minutes today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 2.37 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of May, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
